official_eval.failure_diagnosis: all three: program bug, not physics. The corridor path is sampled on a 5 mm x grid; where it needs a large y change over a tiny x step one segment is up to 0.15 m long; the carrot is capped at (tool projection onto vertices) + 0.03 m, so once the tool reaches the far end of the long segment's first 3 cm its vertex projection does not advance and the carrot freezes; the tool rests at the command (load 0.3-0.6 N) until time-out. Detectable offline: 14/200 snapshot layouts have a gap > 0.03 m under v2 (I did not check this before submitting). Fix in policy_v3 (static check: 0/200), not evaluated.

conclusion_installation: A ~1.0 m inextensible cable/chain (20 markers, 0.052 m apart, lying on the table, radius ~4 mm) clamped at point 1 = (0.05, 0); the tool holds point 20 and drags it around three fixed pegs. The load reading behaves like the pulling force at the tool: ~0.3-0.8 N at rest, rising with dragging speed and with the length of cable in motion (table friction/drag) and stepping up each time the cable wraps a peg (capstan friction). At <= 0.1 m/s with load-based throttling it never exceeded 5.3 N; the cable follows the tool's route and stays wrapped when the tool stops.
